scope: Historical cluster series plus all 11 publicly identified LC24 data-center loads (840 MW) and all 3 publicly identified serial San Jose data-center loads (700 MW) from PG&E/CAISO public transmission-planning material.
notes: The 14 load-project records are now individually represented. Their coordinates are planning-area display points based on the public load-pocket geography; they are not exact facility addresses. Historical generator queue clusters remain a distinct non-additive history layer.

scope: Current public endpoint exposes 83 additional >=100 MW requests in the captured dataset but the required state/location fields are absent from the public response used by this registry.
notes: The 83 are held outside row-level core and included only in expanded-known accounting. MISO also states detailed project information is constrained until a GIA is filed with FERC.

scope: PJM publicly exposes serial and cycle service-request tables for generation, merchant transmission and long-term firm transmission service. The public generation tables are not a large-load queue; a separate public per-load-request dataset was not established.
notes: Historical/current service-request evolution is documented; large-load aggregate transparency remains subject to the FERC proceeding and PJM publication process.

scope: ERCOT Batch Zero applies to eligible >=75 MW large loads; September 2026 verification RFIs were issued to a majority of conditionally included ILLEs. ERCOT's public process page publishes forms and guidance, but completed RFI responses are not an open per-project dataset.
notes: No individual Batch Zero rows are invented. Monthly GIS remains the public generator-side interconnection dataset, distinct from large-load intake.

scope: SPP publishes a detailed active generator-interconnection listing and a dedicated HILL framework for large loads, including data centers. The public HILL page provides process/study architecture rather than a per-load customer table.
notes: The load/customer layer is preserved as process and filing evidence; SPP MDAG materials confirm the HILL/HILLGA processes are operating under FERC-approved Docket ER26-247, but the public HILL page does not enumerate a complete customer-level load table.

scope: NYISO publishes a dedicated Load Projects tab in its public interconnection queue. Independent current-readable mirrors expose queue ID, developer, project, MW, county and POI; 12 named load projects are now linked into the project-level extraction layer.
notes: The accessible public universe remains larger than the 12 individually mapped records in this first crosswalk; the source population and accounting are retained rather than claiming a complete facility match.

scope: ISO-NE's public 2026 large-load forecast names a 200 MW data-center project in NEMA and an additional large electrification project, but does not provide the per-project maturity/status ladder needed for a full study-stage history.
notes: Public forecast/project identity evidence is preserved; no study stage is inferred from forecast inclusion.

scope: All 28 Data Load rows from the retained September 2026 queue extraction now have project IDs, names, requested/contract-capacity values and public planning-area/town identities in the project layer.
notes: The public row still does not identify the commercial customer/proponent for these 28 projects. That field remains explicitly unknown rather than inferred.

scope: IESO application status publishes a large connection universe with applicant, name, zone, type, size, target date and status. Six current load/increase-load records are now in the project layer.
notes: Technical feasibility reports may be confidential; OEB CCIM is preserved as a distribution-capacity context layer rather than a fabricated customer list.

scope: Utility, regulator and permit sources beyond the nine organized markets are preserved as discrete projects where public identity is exposed, plus non-additive aggregate demand/service evidence.
notes: Project-level layer now includes 33 Virginia DEQ permits, 35 BPA large-load request records, 28 AESO data-load projects, 12 NYISO load projects, six IESO load applications, eight AEP named projects, two EEI projects, and three named utility-service/contract/distribution records.
